notes: Complete fix with Token and parser helpers; tests mostly check only that parsing succeeds and segment counts.
Correct at all sites using Token helpers plus thin parser wrappers; the tests parse several inputs and verify a quoted brace is dispensed as an argument.
Misses the nesting-tracking checks inside NextBlock, so a quoted '}' or '{' ending a line still changes nesting when tokens are walked; its tests hide this by consuming args with RemainingArgs.
Correct via Dispenser helpers plus inline checks in doImport/addresses; the TestParseAll addition only asserts keys, though the dispenser test checks args.
Leaves ArgErr and the doImport anonymous-block check unchanged, so quoted braces are still misclassified there; tests are mostly success-only.
Fixes the main parsing paths but leaves ArgErr and the import anonymous-block check comparing Val() without considering quotes; the tests include snippet import.
Leaves ArgErr unchanged, so a quoted '{' gets a misleading error message, and the only test checks site keys in TestParseAll.
Clean Token helpers but ArgErr is not updated; the only test added is a TestParseAll case that checks keys, not segment contents.
Code changes are complete, but there are only three count-based tests.
Correct and complete with Dispenser helpers and inline checks elsewhere, but the tests are minimal (three count-only table cases).
Functionally complete, but the `&& !Quoted()` condition is repeated inline at every site instead of in a helper, and the tests only check segment counts.
Correct at all sites, but repeats `&& !Token().Quoted()` inline everywhere instead of factoring a helper; the table tests are adequate.
Complete fix with very thorough tests: dispenser, segments, snippets, unbalanced-brace errors and an adapt fixture.
Complete helper-based fix (redundant wasQuoted check retained); extensive tests cover segments, snippets, unbalanced braces and adapt output.
Complete Token-helper approach that keeps one redundant wasQuoted check; tests verify segment contents, including snippet import.

Unquoted-brace Token helpers are applied at every structural site, matching the reference; it keeps a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive() and misses the quoted HasSuffix and "{}" refinements; dispenser and segment-level parse tests are good.
Uses inline checks everywhere but misses the anonymous-block check in doImport, so a quoted '{' mapping key still errors; tests are count-only.
Inline quoted checks are repeated throughout with no helper, the import anonymous-block check is missed, and the redundant check is kept; the tests are adequate.
Misses the anonymous-block check in doImport and mixes helpers with inline checks; tests check segments but are otherwise modest.
Dispenser helpers fix the main paths but miss the import anonymous-block check; the subtests verify segments well.
Complete fix with thorough tests covering keys, segments, an unbalanced-brace error case, import blocks and an adapt fixture.
Clean Token-helper fix at all sites; the very thorough tests include an unbalanced-error case, snippet/import blocks and an adapt test.
Complete and clean, but adds a server-spinning integration test on top of solid unit tests.
Complete and correct helper-based fix, though addresses uses an inline check inconsistently; dispenser, parse and end-to-end integration tests are thorough but the integration test spins up a server.
Complete fix with Token and dispenser helpers; tests are count-based table entries.
Correct and complete, using both Token and bounds-checked Dispenser helpers (slightly redundant layering); the table tests cover the issue and nested cases.
Complete, clean Token-helper fix that drops the redundant check; tests are count-based table entries.
Clean Token helpers applied everywhere, with the redundant inner wasQuoted check removed; the table tests cover the issue and a nested block but only check token counts.
Complete fix with Token helpers and at* dispenser wrappers, plus thorough dispenser and parse table tests.
Thorough fix with Token and Dispenser helpers at every site; the dispenser test verifies args, nesting and landing token, and the parse table covers backticks and nesting.
Complete and clean, with a good NextBlock test that puts a quoted '}' alone on its own line and verifies nesting returns to 0.
Complete fix with Token and Dispenser helpers; the dispenser test usefully covers a standalone quoted "}" line inside a block.
Covers every brace check the reference touches, using Token helpers plus dispenser wrappers (the bounds checks are redundant), and adds good dispenser, segment and snippet tests.
Complete fix with consistent helpers at every site; the dispenser and segment-level parse tests include backticks, nested blocks and snippets.
Complete fix that mixes dispenser helpers with inline wasQuoted checks and keeps a now-redundant wasQuoted test; tests cover the dispenser, segments and snippets.
Correct with bounds-checked Dispenser helpers and inline checks elsewhere (keeps a redundant wasQuoted check); the dispenser and segment-level parse tests are good.
Same per-config-resource override flaw, and its refactoring test asserts that the child's distinct ["q"] import is dropped, locking in the silent-drop behavior.
Config-level override with an unrelated path-copy tweak. Its unit test asserts that a child block for a different instance is dropped, which is the wrong behavior.
Quadratic linear scan over all statements to detect overrides, with the same coarse cross-module dropping.
Keeps all same-module blocks via an O(n^2) scan. It still drops every child block for a resource whenever any parent block targets it, rather than deduplicating per instance.
Fixes the reported single-module scenario, but per-config-resource override across modules still drops unrelated child instance imports.
Pointer-slice version of the config-level claim approach. It fixes root-module for_each imports but not per-instance parent/child resolution.
Same ownership-map fix with coarse cross-module override; the test dereferences Importing without a nil check, so a regression panics instead of reporting.
Same claimed-map approach. It fixes the reported scenario but keeps whole-resource override across modules; the test dereferences `Importing` without a nil check.
Map of slices fixes the issue's example but keeps parent-overrides-whole-resource semantics that lose child-module imports.
Another map-of-slices variant. It fixes same-module for_each imports but keeps the config-level parent override.
Map-of-slices variant that fixes same-module for_each imports but keeps per-config-resource parent override.
Changes the return type to a map of slices so same-module blocks survive. A parent block still overrides all child blocks for the whole resource.
Fixes same-module for_each imports, but its fixture expects the child's distinct ["c"] instance import to be discarded, enshrining the silent-drop class of bug.

Fixes the same-module case. It still overrides at the config-resource level, so a parent block for one instance silently drops child blocks for other instances, and its new unit test encodes that drop.
Moves override to instance level by statically re-parsing `to` keys, but falls back to dropping blocks whenever a key is dynamic and ignores module instance keys, which is heuristic and incomplete.

Overrides per instance when keys are statically known by re-parsing `To` traversals. It ignores module instance keys and falls back to whole-resource override for dynamic targets, leaving some silent drops.
Module-ownership map fixes the reported case but still discards whole sets of child-module imports when a parent targets any instance of the same resource.
Claimed-map fix plus a defensive path copy. Parent/child override still drops other instances' child blocks.
Map of slices keeps every same-module block, but override is still per config resource, so child-module blocks for instances the parent never targets are silently dropped.
Map-of-slices variant that is equivalent to C11 and carries the same whole-resource override limitation.
Ownership-map approach retains same-module blocks but keeps coarse cross-module override that can still silently drop child imports.
Same config-level claim approach with a clear comment. It fixes the issue scenario only.
Same ownership approach using a string-keyed map instead of addrs.Map; good fixture and context tests, but the cross-module instance-level override is still wrong.
String-keyed owners map with the same whole-resource override flaw. The unit and plan tests are reasonable.
Same O(n^2) override scan as C14; fixes the reported case but still drops child-module instance imports.
Linear-scan variant with the same config-level override flaw. A parent block for one instance discards child blocks for other instances.

Removes config-level dedup and orders child modules before parents so the later knownImports.Put gives parent precedence per instance; this matches the reference semantics, though it relies implicitly on overwrite order.

Removes config-level dedup and orders children before parents so the overwriting Put lets parent blocks win per instance. This matches the reference semantics, though it relies implicitly on overwrite order, and the only test covers the root-module case.
Clean ownership-map fix for same-module for_each imports; cross-module override remains too coarse.
Clean owners-map fix for the root-module case. Cross-module override is still per config resource, not per instance, unlike the intended behavior.
Ownership-map fix whose test also covers multi-instance imports inside a child module, but there is no override test and cross-module dedup is still too coarse.
Config-level claim fix. The test also covers multi-block imports inside a child module, but override semantics remain per config resource.
Pointer-slice ownership approach that fixes the issue example but still silently drops child imports when a parent targets the same config resource.
Containing-module map approach fixes the reported case. Cross-module resolution is still per config resource, not per instance.

Fixes the single-module for_each case, but parent precedence is still decided per config resource, so a child block for an instance the parent never names (child imports ["y"], parent imports only ["x"]) is still silently dropped; tests cover multi-instance and a simple override.
Correct for same-module blocks and has decent unit and plan tests. Cross-module override remains at config-resource granularity.
Reaches into treePages directly and only rewrites a regular page's dir when it equals the section base, so pages in nested non-section dirs miss the slug; this fails a hidden test.
Reaches into pageMap.treePages directly, which is hacky, and only rewrites regular pages that sit directly in their section, so descendants in subdirectories keep the untranslated path.
Lowercase prefix-map replacement is correct for nested dirs, but the function returns an error it never produces and uses type assertions where Slug() would do.
Works through a lowercased prefix map, but has a pointless always-nil error return, a pageState type assertion, and the same normalization-mismatch caveat.
A depth-keyed slug map applied to SectionBase or ContainerDir works for nested dirs; it adds two descriptor fields and the test lacks non-section subdirectory coverage.
Depth-to-slug map applied to section base or container dir; correct and reasonably clean.
Deliberately skips slugs for pages not directly in their section and when the section depth does not match the path, so descendants in nested dirs keep the untranslated URL; this fails a hidden test.
Bails out when a regular page is not directly in its section or when the section chain doesn't map 1:1 to path segments, so many descendants don't get the slug.

Builds a lowercase prefix-to-slug map from ancestors (plus the page itself for branches) and rewrites Section.Base or ContainerDir, which correctly handles nested dirs and skipped section levels; the test does not cover non-section subdirectories.
Prefix-map replacement handles nested dirs; lowercasing unnormalized segments to compare with normalized Path() can mismatch under disablePathToLower (e.g. spaces).
The prefix-map replacement is correct, but feeding the result through ExpandedPermalink (bypassing its unescape/clean) misuses the permalink-config path.
Works by building the full path and stuffing it into ExpandedPermalink, which overloads permalink semantics and is fragile.

Reuses the ExpandedPermalink mechanism to inject slugged paths, which is hacky and emits permalink debug logs; a slugged section also drops intermediate non-section directories between it and its parent.
Builds the slugged path, correctly handling multi-segment section paths, but routes it through the permalink branch, so it gets query-unescaped and treated as an ExpandedPermalink, which is hacky.

Regular pages always use the slugged section path in place of their container dir, so pages in non-section subdirectories (e.g. help/x/p.md) silently lose those directory segments; a slug also drops any intermediate directories.
Replaces a regular page's whole container dir with the slugged section path, dropping intermediate subdirectories, which gives wrong and potentially colliding URLs.
Depth-based replacement is computed only when no permalink or URL applies, and is correct for nested dirs; the new test file lacks a license header and non-section-subdir coverage.
Depth-indexed slug replacement applied only when no permalink or url is set; clean and correct for nested and unnormalized paths.
A clean Slugs map on the descriptor, with applySlugs prefix-replacing segments in both section and container paths, is correct for nested dirs and disablePathToLower.
Clean slug map keyed by normalized/unnormalized base and applied by prefix in CreateTargetPaths; handles nested dirs and taxonomies.
A SectionSlugs map keyed by section base, applied in CreateTargetPaths to both section base and container dir, is clean and handles nested dirs; tests are adequate but miss non-section subdirs.
Passes a slug map keyed by the consistently (un)normalized section base into the descriptor and applies it by prefix in CreateTargetPaths; robust.
Walks CurrentSection to Parent collecting slugs, then does prefix-matched replacement on the dir, which is clean and correct for nested dirs; tests miss non-section subdirectories.
Section-chain slug map with prefix matching handles nested dirs and skips home/standalone pages; it has a minor normalization caveat with disablePathToLower.
Depth-based replacement via SectionsEntries correctly keeps intermediate non-section dirs, and tests cover nested dirs with a skipped level, uglyURLs, and taxonomy/term slugs.
SectionsEntries-depth replacement is simple and correct; the tests cover nested non-section dirs, ugly URLs and taxonomy/term slugs.

The SectionSlugs map in the descriptor is applied in CreateTargetPaths and handles nested dirs and disablePathToLower, but the unchecked `sp.(*pageState).m.Slug()` type assertion is needless and fragile.
Slug map applied by path prefix in CreateTargetPaths handles nested and unnormalized paths; it uses an unchecked *pageState type assertion.

A concise depth-based replacement walking the CurrentSection to Parent chain with a single Dir field, closest in spirit to the reference, with tests covering deep non-section dirs and taxonomy/term slugs.
Concise walk from CurrentSection up via Parent with depth-indexed replacement and a cmp.Or fallback; the two tests cover deep non-section dirs and taxonomy/term slugs.
Depth-indexed slug replacement on Section.Base or ContainerDir is correct and the test covers a nested plain dir, but it also edits documentation files the task did not require.

Index-based slug substitution over ancestors plus self works for nested non-section dirs and unnormalized paths, the test is thorough, and the docs edits are accurate but go beyond what the task needed.

Correctly appends the remainder for nested non-section dirs, but rebuilding the section path from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier drops intermediate directories whenever a section's parent is not its immediate dir.
Rebuilds the path from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, which drops intermediate non-section dirs between sections (e.g. help/sub/deep with no sub/_index); otherwise sound.
Returns no slug path for pages not directly in their current section, and a slug replaces the whole relative segment including skipped dirs; this fails a hidden test.
Branch paths are correct, but regular pages not directly in their current section are skipped, so their URLs keep the untranslated section name.
Reference-like wrapDurationExpr refactor that works, but it adds an awkward parenPos parameter (passed as 0 when unused) and omits the Pretty fix.
Clean unified `wrapDurationExpr` close to the reference, at the cost of an extra position parameter; Pretty and the parse-time checks are not addressed.
Correct, focused fix using a recursive applyUnaryOp call; it has no Pretty fix and does not keep the parse-time zero-duration error.
Small, correct wrapping in both paths that uses the paren position; no Pretty change, and the positive and div-by-zero checks move to eval time.
Complete fix with the Pretty unary-plus correction and positive-duration validation for (0) and -(5), backed by error and printer tests.
Correct wrapping with the Pretty fix and parse-time positive checks for `(0)` and `-(5)`, but div/mod by `(0)` is no longer caught at parse time.
Works, but has an unchecked NumberLiteral type assertion, a stray generated-header change, an extra experimental-flag check, no Pretty fix, and the new positive check is untested.

Works, but uses an unconditional `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion, changes the generated-file header, adds an unrequested experimental-flag check to `offset -(N)`, and only partly keeps the positive-duration check.
Matches the reference including the Pretty unary-plus fix, keeps the parse-time error for foo[(0)], and adds a test for it.
Correct wrapping plus the Pretty fix, but the positive-duration check only catches `(0)`, not `-(5)`, and div-by-`(0)` is no longer caught at parse time.
Works and extends the positive, division and modulo zero checks to wrapped literals, but those extra checks are untested, StartPos is the inner position, and there is no Pretty fix.

Wraps the bare literal in a unary-plus DurationExpr on both paren paths, and a helper keeps the parse-time positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero checks working; it skips the Pretty update and adds no tests for the preserved errors.
Takes a different route by adding a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral plus conversion shims; it round-trips String(), but mixes two mechanisms, changes the AST API, and Pretty prints +(5).
Adds `NumberLiteral.Wrapped` and rewrites its `String()`, converting to a DurationExpr in grammar actions; it is thorough on the checks but is an invasive AST change with dual representations.
Clean reference-style wrapDurationExpr refactor with a useful durationVisitor test; it misses only the Pretty unary-plus fix.
Essentially the reference design with one unified `wrapDurationExpr` used in both paths, plus a useful durationVisitor evaluation test; only the Pretty tweak is missing.
Very small, clean fix with good round-trip tests covering both tables from the issue; it lacks the Pretty fix and the parse-time zero check.
Minimal reference-like fix in both paren paths; it skips the Pretty fix and uses the literal's start position instead of the paren's.
Minimal working fix, but StartPos is the inner literal position rather than the opening paren, the branch duplicates applyUnaryOp logic, and there is no Pretty fix.
Minimal correct fix with explicit wrapped handling in `applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr`; no Pretty change or parse-time constant checks.
Thorough: Pretty fix, positive check for (0) and -(5), AST, error and visitor tests; the unchecked $2.(*NumberLiteral) assertion in paren_duration_expr is fragile.
Good coverage with the Pretty fix, positive checks and thorough tests, but relies on an unconditional `*NumberLiteral` type assertion in `paren_duration_expr`.

Fixes the issue but overreaches: it resolves Range, Step and Offset at parse time for constant expressions, reorders subquery step printing, and adds an experimental-flag check that changes behaviour.

Fixes the round-trip but expands into computing static Range/Offset/Step for constant expressions, reorders subquery printer precedence, and adds an experimental check; all of this is beyond the issue.
Minimal and correct, but StartPos is the inner literal position rather than the opening paren and there is no Pretty fix.
Same minimal approach as C15 without the redundant range check; correct but leaves Pretty and the parse-time checks unaddressed.

Adds a Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and converts it to a DurationExpr in offset and range positions; this works and keeps the zero checks naturally, but it is more invasive than needed and Pretty prints +(5).

Adds a public `Wrapped` field to NumberLiteral and changes its `String()`, then converts it to a DurationExpr at selected consumer sites; this hybrid representation is more invasive and fragile than needed.
Correct and well tested including eval and error cases, but the wrapping DurationExpr is constructed inline in two places instead of a helper, and there is no Pretty fix.
Wraps on both paren paths and keeps the positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero errors at parse time; tests cover error cases and promqltest evaluation, but the Pretty update is missing.
Solid fix with a safe helper and positive-duration validation, plus strong parse, printer and promqltest eval tests; it does not fix Pretty().
Wraps on both paths with the paren position and keeps the positive-duration errors, with good parse, printer and promqltest coverage; div/mod by `(0)` and Pretty are not handled.
Works and extends the zero checks, but it uses an odd *Item parameter in place of a bool and leaves an altered goyacc header line in the generated file.
Complete fix that keeps all parse-time checks, but changes `applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr` to take an awkward `*Item` and includes regenerated-header noise.

Fixes both the paren and unary-paren paths with a clear helper and restores the parse-time positive-duration check for (0) and -(5); it misses the Pretty() unary-plus fix, so prettified output becomes (+5).
Correct wrapping with the paren position and a positive-duration constant check; div/mod by `(0)` and Pretty are not handled.
Compact implementation in internal/cmd with archive and unit tests; there is no run-level integration test, and exec is always serialized as explicitly set.
Compact internal/cmd implementation that works, but exec is always marked valid ("default"), and there is no end-to-end run test, only unit and archive tests.
Works, but it puts a CLI-specific OnceConflictError helper in the public lib/executor package, and the bool return of applyOnceFlag only feeds a debug log.
Works, but puts a CLI flag error helper (OnceConflictError) in lib/executor, uses an awkward if/else debug-log pattern, and always sets exec as valid.
Straightforward and correct for the main paths; its tests rely on summary output and cover neither the archive nor the tags.
Clean DeriveOnceScenario after consolidation; tests are adequate, but the env check via a throw is weak and there is no archive test.
ApplyOnce never sets VUs and Iterations explicitly, so the serialized scenario has null vus and iterations; this breaks hidden tests and the package suite.
ApplyOnce never explicitly sets VUs and iterations to 1 (it relies on invalid defaults), so the serialized config is wrong and hidden tests fail; its own tests mask this by checking only Int64.
Sound post-consolidation transform with conflict checks, but it exports a new lib/executor API and its tests have no archive coverage and only light checks that tags and env are preserved.
Clean flag set and applyOnceFlag with proper exec handling; tests are reasonable but lighter, with no archive check.
Validates conflicts before consolidation and applies ApplyOnce after it, with nil-cmd safety; it has decent tests but no archive test.
Correct ApplyOnce next to the shortcut derivation logic, with basic integration and unit tests, but no archive or setup/teardown coverage.

Correct, lists all conflicting flags in the error and has very thorough tests, including struct-equality and non-mutation checks; conflict validation is split into loadAndConfigureLocalTest, which is slightly fragile.
Correct post-consolidation ApplyOnce with good tests, but conflict validation and application are split across two call sites, and a CLI-specific '--once' error lives in lib/executor.

Checks conflicts through the parsed CLI options, builds the scenario through a clear helper, and has extensive tests including exit codes, derivation idempotence and the archive; clearing Duration only via Valid is a small fragility.
Thorough tests, including DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts stability and archive, but conflict detection is inferred indirectly from parsed CLI options, and BaseConfig construction is convoluted.
Works, but it silently ignores the GetBool error, clears shortcuts only by flipping Valid, and its integration tests are light with no archive coverage.
Functional, but silently discards the GetBool error, and tests are shallow (output-string checks only, no archive or setup/teardown coverage).
Minimal and correct implementation in config.go, but it only has unit tests and no end-to-end run or archive verification.
Correct logic kept in config.go with proper exec handling and exit codes, but tests are unit-only, with no run or archive coverage.

Well-structured implementation with flags on run, archive and cloud, and thorough tests including metric-tag preservation, archive metadata and Validate checks; it shares the unhandled lower-layer shortcut edge case.
Separate flag set wired into run, archive, and cloud, with ApplyOnce applied post-consolidation; strong tests verify env/tags via metric tags, setup/teardown, and archive metadata.

Correctly rewrites the consolidated scenario to shared-iterations 1/1, keeping exec/env/tags/options, and wires the flag into run, archive and cloud run; it adds a new public executor API, misses the case where env or file shortcuts wipe scenarios during the merge, and has strong tests.
Sound applyOnceFlag wrapper over executor.ApplyOnce, added to run, archive, and cloud run; thorough tests, though it reinvents strings.Count with a custom helper.

Self-contained implementation in internal/cmd with a separate flag set on run, archive and cloud, with thorough unit, integration and archive tests; like the others it ignores lower-layer shortcuts that clobber scenarios during consolidation.

Well-structured once.go in internal/cmd with a separate flag set for run, archive, and cloud; very thorough tests, including shorthand-flag conflicts, setup/teardown, and archive round-trip via ReadArchive.
Well-contained once.go that names the conflicting scenarios and sets exit codes, with comprehensive unit, integration and archive tests that also check script-level vus is discarded.

Self-contained once.go applies --once after consolidation, preserves exec/env/tags/options, and rejects conflicting and multiple-scenario cases with InvalidConfig; tests cover unit, run, and archive paths, but shortcuts from lower layers can still wipe scenarios during the merge.
Clean ApplyOnce in execution_config_shortcuts.go plus a flag check in test_load; it works for the main cases, lacks an archive test, and duplicates the existing sum helper.
Straightforward ApplyOnce in lib/executor with conflict checks; integration tests verify iteration counts with scenario tags, but there is no archive test.
Clean, with early flag validation and good integration tests (including discarding startTime and checking JSON tag output), but no archive test.
Clean implementation; the integration test with startTime '1h' nicely proves extra fields are discarded, but there is no archive test.

Functionally correct, but the scenario construction is clumsy (NewBaseConfig with a hardcoded type, then overwriting BaseConfig) and the `!= ""` exec check is dead logic that always marks exec as set.
Works, but builds the scenario via BaseConfig with a string literal, always marks exec valid, and its archive test uses a no-scenario script so preservation isn't verified.
Works and has good run, archive and unit tests, but it introduces an unnecessary new error type instead of reusing ExecutionConflictError and puts CLI messaging in lib/executor.
Works and has good run and archive tests, but introduces an unnecessary new OnceScenarioError type in lib/executor instead of reusing existing error types.

Traps the wrapped `ExecError` at template boundaries but does not protect against `try` swallowing returns, has no `HasValue` (bare return yields nil), uses an ad-hoc pipeline reordering transform, and leaves a leftover `x` helper func and a sloppy comment.
Relies on ExecError wrapping instead of a direct panic, so try swallows return; a bare return gives nil, and the pipeline-reordering rewrite built from dummy parsed templates is convoluted.

Avoids exec changes by unwrapping the error from `ExecError`, which is clever, but `try` swallows the return, there is no template-boundary trap (a return in `define "main"` truncates baseof), and it edits upstream `parse/node.go`.
Leaves the executor untouched, so try swallows return and define/block returns kill the page, and it patches the forked parse package, which adds fork-maintenance burden.
Clean `HasValue` and `try` handling with a nice shortcode test, but it is missing the `walkTemplate` trap, so returns inside `block`/`template` terminate the whole outer template.
Good HasValue, try and arg-wrap handling with solid tests, but has no walkTemplate trap, so an early return in a define "main" block kills the baseof output.
Correct sentinel flow with `try` handling and a bare return yielding the output so far, but with no `walkTemplate` trap a bare return inside a `block`/`define` ends the entire outer template.
Correct partial semantics with HasValue and a try fix, plus unit and integration tests, but return inside template/block invocations unwinds the entire outer template.

Functionally strong, with a template trap, `try` handling, `HasValue` and good unit plus integration tests, but more intrusive: it changes the `Executer` interface and the `executeWithState` signature.

Clean separate return channel through the executer, with walkTemplate trap, try fix, HasValue and smart arg wrapping plus thorough unit and integration tests; it widens the Executer interface, which is more invasive to the fork.
Keeps `HasReturn`, so any partial containing a return discards its output and a bare return yields nil; there is no `walkTemplate` trap, so a return inside a `block`/`template` ends the whole page.
Keeps HasReturn and io.Discard, so a partial that never reaches its return gives nil; a bare return also gives nil, and return inside define/block kills the whole baseof render.
Correct `HasValue` and `walkTemplate` trapping with good tests, but `try` swallows the return and the tests enshrine silently ignoring commands after return in a pipeline.
Core behaviour is correct (walkTemplate trap, HasValue), but it misses the try re-panic so try swallows return, and a test codifies silently dropping the rest of a pipeline after return.
Traps returns in `executeWithState` and `walkTemplate` and handles `try`, but keeps `HasReturn` output-discarding, so a bare or unreached return yields nil rather than the rendered output.
Traps return in walkTemplate and executeWithState with a try fix, but keeps HasReturn with output discard and has no HasValue, so partials never return rendered output once they contain a return.

Well-structured: `HasValue`, `try` re-panic, `walkTemplate` trap, `errors.As` at the store boundary, an arity check and thorough tests; it shares the trap-all-at-template-boundary and silent-pipeline gaps.

Sound sentinel-error design: walkTemplate trap, try re-panic, HasValue so a bare return yields the rendered output, and arg wrapping; it silently ignores values outside partials and does not reject a non-final return in a pipeline.

Handles the shorthand in `evalFunction` like the reference, but has no template-boundary trap, a bare return yields nil, it adds an unrequested `_returnNoop` decorator rewrite, and it loses the transform error context.

Has no walkTemplate trap and no HasValue, and adds a _returnNoop function plus AST neutralisation for decorator else-branches, which reintroduces the transformation complexity the issue wanted removed.

Solid sentinel-panic design: `try` re-panics the return, `walkTemplate` traps it, and a bare return yields the partial's output so far; however, it traps valued returns at template boundaries too, silently ignores pipelines after return, moves the `return` alias into the templates namespace, and edits fork files without updating the fork script.
Same solid approach as the best candidates and moves return into the templates namespace with good tests, but adds docs churn and silently ignores extra arguments and non-final pipeline returns.

Clean implementation with `HasValue`, `try` re-panic, `walkTemplate` trap, an arity check and good integration tests; it moves `return` into the templates namespace, changes the `ExecuteWithContextAndKey` signature, and traps valued returns at template boundaries.
Solid: walkTemplate trap, try fix, HasValue, arg grouping and good block/template/pipe tests, with return moved to the templates namespace.
Dropping all transforms without arg-wrapping breaks the existing `return add . 42` shorthand, and a bare return yields nil rather than the rendered output.
Drops arg wrapping, so the existing `{{ return add . 42 }}` form breaks, and has no HasValue, so a bare return in a partial yields nil.
Breaks the `return add . 42` shorthand, keeps `HasReturn` output discarding with nil for bare returns, and lacks `try` protection.
Has no arg wrapping, so `return add . 42` breaks, no try fix and no HasValue; it keeps HasReturn, which discards output.
No `walkTemplate` trap and a bare return yields nil; it rewrites `return X | f` into a nested pipeline, contrary to the intended error, and renames and repurposes an existing regression test.
Has no walkTemplate trap and no HasValue, changes pipeline semantics so `return X | Y` returns the whole pipeline, and rewrites the existing 13600 regression test to fit.
Good `HasValue` semantics and a template-boundary trap via the `walkReturnable` helper, but `try` still swallows the return panic and the docs add dangling reference links.
Correct walkTemplate trap and HasValue semantics with good tests, but it misses the try re-panic, changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature, and leaves dangling doc link references.
